### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-approvals`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **4** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/liveness/field.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**5** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/approvals.mdx`  _(via actor_id (literal, a string literal in regions), sys_approval_action (literal, a string literal in regions))_
- `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx`  _(via sys_approval_action (literal, a string literal in regions))_
- `content/docs/automation/workflows.mdx`  _(via sys_approval_action (literal, a string literal in regions))_
- `content/docs/frontend/plugins/plugin-detail.mdx`  _(via actor_id (literal, a string literal in regions))_
- `content/docs/plugins/packages.mdx`  _(via sys_approval_action (literal, a string literal in regions))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via sys_approval_action (literal, a string literal in regions))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-7.mdx`  _(via actor_id (literal, a string literal in regions), sys_approval_action (literal, a string literal in regions))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/liveness/field.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `created_at (literal, 46 pages)`
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **173** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d57d6eedbb940257cc4d7604a26f407841f65bc7` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `23e4529aef545a48f1d1ed29ea7a5dc838271e7c` — the merge of head `5539896777e2a43bb628746738ebd2b96707c9d3` into base `d57d6eedbb940257cc4d7604a26f407841f65bc7`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 23e4529aef545a48f1d1ed29ea7a5dc838271e7c && git checkout 23e4529aef545a48f1d1ed29ea7a5dc838271e7c
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin d57d6eedbb940257cc4d7604a26f407841f65bc7 5539896777e2a43bb628746738ebd2b96707c9d3 && git checkout -B drift-repro d57d6eedbb940257cc4d7604a26f407841f65bc7 && git merge --no-ff 5539896777e2a43bb628746738ebd2b96707c9d3

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d57d6eedbb940257cc4d7604a26f407841f65bc7
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs d57d6eedbb940257cc4d7604a26f407841f65bc7` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

### Must-fix

None.

### Should-fix

None.

### Readings that hold

| Item | Reading |
|:--|:--|
| PR shape | Draft, base `main`, `Fixes #34588` (the card's own PR, all four 要做的 items). No `!`, no `(narrowing)`: no dogfood battery owed. |
| Scope | 32 files, all inside the claim plus its three amendments: `plugin-approvals/src/**` (the page and its test); `app-shell/src/views/**` (the panel, `SubmittedRecord.tsx` + `submittedRecordPlan.ts` (+ test) replacing `RecordSnapshotSummary.tsx` + `snapshotSummaryPlan.ts` (+ test), `approval-progress/ApprovalActionTimeline.tsx` shared with `RecordApprovalsPanel.tsx`, three rewritten panel suites, the new `fullRecord-34588` suite); `app-shell/README.md` (6937866666); `spec/liveness/field.json` (6938072917, evidence clause only); `openPathObjectReaders-12811.test.ts` (6938514752, one `off` row); the two console `servedPage*` tests (test-only, in the claim); 11 locale files; the changeset. |
| The page | `sys_approval_request_detail` now authors `page:header` → `record:highlights` → `record:approval_decision`, with no `page:tabs`, `record:details` or `record:related_list`. The header doc comment was rewritten to match, line for line. The highlight strip still drops `record_id`, now because the panel draws the target record, not a details-grid card. |
| Acceptance 1 (whole record, sections, child rows) | `planSubmittedRecord` walks `deriveRecordDetailSections` (the object's default record-page derivation, field groups resolved through `deriveFieldGroupDetailSections`). It draws every declared, non-`hidden`, non-system field that either row serves, so the six-row cap is gone. Child tables are `deriveRelatedLists` filtered to `isPrimary \|\| isOwned`, gated on the child's read verdict, drawn once the record read, each with the "current rows" note. Pinned past six fields, with child rows. |
| Acceptance 2 (Changed) | One `findOne(objectName, recordId)` with no params (pinned as the only call), re-read on data-bus invalidation. `valuesDiffer` compares references by id (bare or expanded), numbers numerically, dates by instant, lists as sets, and all empties as one, so a served-expanded lookup does not falsely read as changed. Exactly one changed field is marked in the pin, with its current value. An unreadable record marks nothing and says so (CONTROL pin). |
| Acceptance 3 (FLS) | Both rows pass `withoutDeniedFields(row, perms, target)` before planning, on top of the service's per-reader `payload` redaction; a `hidden: true` field is dropped as well. Pinned from both rows: neither the label nor the value of a denied or hidden field appears anywhere in the panel. |
| Rail order | `approval-decision-rail` children are exactly `[progress, submitted-attachments, activity]` (pinned), activity last, as the maintainer asked. The activity reads `sys_approval_action` only when `perms.can(..., 'read')` allows it. Attachment fields leave the field grid for the rail card. The decision band sits above both columns (pinned by document position). |
| Nothing editable | Child tables are the plugin's `RelatedList` with no create/edit/delete/row handlers passed (pinned: no New / Add buttons). Snapshot storage is untouched: no service or schema change. |
| Delta line (the merge `55398967`) | The merge resolves one conflict in `ApprovalDecisionPanel.tsx`: against the pre-merge parent `55785f05` it adds only #34641's two-line comment and `foldDecisions` on the `DeclaredActionsBar` call site (now about line 441). The props match `main`'s call site exactly (`objectName`, `record`, `location`, `onDone`, `foldDecisions`). This is the delta read the seat asked the second lander to owe. |
| Shared timeline | `RecordApprovalsPanel` now renders `ApprovalActionTimeline` with its own rows and step resolver; the request page passes its thread newest first. There is one markup for both, which keeps the earlier timeline behaviour: kinds, override rows, reassignment from/to, signed-URL attachments, display-locale dates. |
| Rewritten pins | Each removed assertion pins the retired surface: the six-row cut, the amount lead, the Details/Timeline tabs, the related list's `step_label` column. The PR body pairs each with its replacement and the card line that retires it. No pin of a kept behaviour was dropped without a successor: FLS, step text, the decision band and the snapshot heading "As submitted" are all re-pinned in the new suites. |
| Clause-② / Metadata-protocol | `yes (widening — new @object-ui/i18n locale keys only)` / `none`, the same in claim, body and changeset. Seven add-only `approvalsInbox.*` keys, present in all 11 packs (7 lines each; zh-Hant regenerated by `gen:zh-hant`). zh-Hans: 已改动 / 当前值 / 打开记录 / 无法读取当前记录，提交后的改动无法标出。/ 当前值：提交时未保存子表数据。/ 审批进度 / 附件. `@object-ui/app-shell` is private, and `SubmittedRecord` and `submittedRecordPlan` are module-internal. `@objectstack/plugin-approvals` changes a page's node list, which is product metadata, not an accept set. The liveness edit repoints evidence only (status and verifiedAt are unchanged). This is locale-keys-only, so per the seat's routing L1-a reads it at TIER_DEFAULT, and no further L2 is owed. |
| Changeset | `patch` for `@objectstack/plugin-approvals`, `@object-ui/app-shell` and `@object-ui/i18n`, the three packages whose `src` moved (console and spec change no src). Every sentence matches the readings above, including "reads the target record once (`findOne`, no params)", "the activity is read only when the reader's verdict allows reading that object", and the seven key names. |
| Docs | `content/docs/automation/approvals.mdx:1055` ("both approval step lines … the record's approvals panel and the request page") stays true. No docs page describes the request page's tabs or the six-field summary. The app-shell README section was rewritten to the shipped layout (amendment 6937866666). |
| Tests | Real commands with output: post-merge vitest over i18n, approval-decision, the #34361/#25877 fold suites, `RecordDetailView.approval*`, the reader census and the console data-source suites, 134 files / 2171 passed, exit 0. eslint on the panel exit 0. 78 derived gates: 76 exit 0, and 2 NOT-MEASURED (`check:dual-build-cjs-loads` and `check:published-readme-exports` need a full build, which CI's Build Core runs). |

### CI

67 check-runs on this exact head (the merge `55398967`): all `success` or `skipped`, none pending. Test Core 8/8 shards plus the aggregate, Test UI 16/16 plus the aggregate, Build Core (which covers the two NOT-MEASURED build gates), Build & E2E UI, Live E2E UI, Type Check UI, Lint UI, TypeScript Type Check, Lint & Repo Gates, Spec property liveness, Check Changeset, PR-body guards and Governed Surface Queue Guard are all `success`. The pre-merge head `55785f05` was also all green (66 runs, per the report).

### Notes

1. **Tier H routing.** I am handing this to the seat as Tier H. It is not readied from here.
2. A field that the current row serves but the snapshot does not (for example, one added to the object after submission) is drawn empty and marked Changed with its current value. That reads correctly as "not part of the submission, has a value now", but it is the one case where "Changed" means "added".
3. The child-table read gate uses `perms.can(child, 'read')` only once permissions have loaded; before that, the server's own refusal is the gate. That is the same as `deriveRelatedLists` elsewhere.
4. Not driven in a browser here. If the maintainer wants a look before approving, a request on a 10+ field object with a child table in showcase covers all three acceptance lines on one page.
